description.narrative:
Safe Play, Strong Voices is a 12-month youth-led advocacy project implemented by Youth for Change Network in Nakuru County to promote inclusive, safe, and non-discriminatory sporting spaces for LBQ (lesbian, bisexual, and queer) and Gender Non-Conforming(GNC) young athletes aged 18–35. The project responds to persistent stigma, harassment, and exclusion that limit the participation and leadership of marginalised youth in sports.
The project will strengthen the voice and leadership of LBQ <(>&<)> GNC athletes through advocacy and safeguarding capacity building, youth-led forums, and structured policy dialogues with county government, sports associations, schools, and civil society actors. By documenting lived experiences and engaging decision-makers, the initiative will generate practical policy recommendations and safeguarding approaches that advance safety and inclusion in sports.
The goal of the project isto promote safe, inclusive, and non-discriminatory sporting spaces for LBQ and Gender Non-Conforming (GNC) young athletes in NakuruCounty. The project objectives are to strengthen youth leadership and advocacy, amplify the voices of marginalized athletes, and influence inclusive sports policies and safeguarding practices. Key activities include youth advocacy and safeguarding capacity building, youth-led forums, policy dialogues with stakeholders, coalition building, documentation of lived experiences, and participation in a global learning exchange.

participating-org.narrative:
Youth for Change Network (YCN) is a youth-led feminist organization based in Nakuru County, Kenya, working to advance the rights, safety, and meaningful participation of marginalized and under-represented young people, particularly LBQ and Gender Non-Conforming (GNC) womxn and youth. YCN was founded to respond to persistent exclusion, violence, and systemic barriers faced by young people at the intersections of gender, sexuality, class, and age.
Vision: A just, inclusive, and equitable society where all young people, regardless of gender identity or sexual orientation, can live safely, participate fully in civic life, and realize their potential.
Mission: To empower marginalize youth through rights-based advocacy, leadership development, community organizing, and policy engagement that centers lived experiences and advances social justice.
Objectives: YCN seeks to (i) strengthen the voice and agency of marginalized youth in decision-making and policy processes; (ii) promote safe, inclusive, and non-discriminatory spaces in community, civic, and public institutions, including sports; (iii) build the leadership, advocacy, and organizing capacity of LBQ <(>&<)> GNC youth; and (iv) foster strategic partnerships and coalitions that advance youth rights and gender justice at local, national, and regional levels.
Values: YCN is guided by feminist principles, youth leadership, intersectionality, accountability, inclusivity, and solidarity. The organization prioritizes safety, dignity, and participation, and is committed to community-led solutions, transparency,and transformative change driven by young people themselves.
